entries.subject: Two matching screws viewed from their shank side, with slotted back faces hidden; two matching spur gears unchanged.
entries.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: transparent hand-painted TECHNOLOGY icon for Victoria 3.
Input images: Image 1 is the edit target, containing two matching screws and two matching spur gear wheels.
Primary request: correct ONLY the physically impossible head perspective on BOTH screws. Their threaded tips point diagonally toward the viewer at lower-right; their thick cylindrical heads are farther away at upper-left. Therefore the slotted screwdriver face is on the FAR BACK side of each head, facing AWAY from the viewer, and must be FULLY HIDDEN.
Show the NEAR-FACING UNDERSIDE of each screw head: a continuous plain annular metal shoulder surrounding the central shank that emerges from it toward the viewer. The shaft and threaded tip remain in their original lower-right direction. Render the head's thickness as a rounded cylindrical rim behind that shoulder, with perspective consistent with the shaft axis. The visible underside is unbroken metal: NO screwdriver slot, groove, cut, cross, socket, hole through the shoulder, or notch. The hidden top face still belongs on the opposite end; do not put the slot on the side wall or threaded tip. This is NOT a screw viewed from its screwdriver side and NOT merely a slot erased on the wrong-facing top face.
Preserve BOTH gear wheels, their silhouettes, teeth, spokes, central bores, relative positions, scale and overlaps. Preserve the two screws' positions, matching dimensions, shafts and threads. Keep the same compact overall composition, natural warm-neutral iron finish, painted grain and soft upper-left lighting. Change only the small head/shoulder areas as needed to make the geometry coherent; do not redesign the group.
Genuine transparent alpha around the group and through gear openings; square canvas at least 1024 pixels. No background, floor, ground shadow, frame, medallion, text, new props, blue/teal tint or sepia filter. Whole group intact and readable at 48/64 pixels.
